definition_zh: 容纳；为……提供住处；顾及；使适应
definition_en: to provide room or lodging for, to have space for, or to adjust to someone's needs
core_image: 把原本放不下的东西挪一挪，硬是留出一个位置
scene: 小礼堂原本只摆得下五十把椅子，会务组把椅子挪紧些，又多塞了二十把。The hall can accommodate seventy guests.
sceneCN: 这里 accommodate 是「容纳」（第 1 个义项：有空间装下）；句意为这个大厅能容纳七十位客人。

pos.zh: 容纳；提供住处；顾及；使适应

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「住处；调适」
由本词加现在分词后缀构成，义为「乐于助人的、通融的」

senses.title: To provide room or lodging
senses.definition: to give someone a place to stay or sit
senses.definitionCN: 给某人提供住或坐的地方
senses.example: The hostel can accommodate forty students.
senses.exampleCN: 这家旅舍能接待四十名学生。
senses.why: Latin accommodare meant 'to fit one thing to another'; providing a bed means fitting a person into a place.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 accommodare 意为「使一物合于另一物」；提供床铺就是把一个人安置进一个地方。

senses.title: To have space for
senses.definition: of a room, vehicle, or container, to hold a certain number or amount
senses.definitionCN: 指房间、车辆或容器能装下一定数量
senses.example: The new stadium accommodates twice as many spectators.
senses.exampleCN: 新体育场能容纳两倍观众。
senses.why: Here the fitting is measured: capacity is the largest number that can be fitted without strain.
senses.whyCN: 这里的「合」是可量化的：容量就是在不勉强的前提下能装下的最大数目。

senses.title: To take account of needs
senses.definition: to adjust arrangements so that someone's needs are met
senses.definitionCN: 调整安排以满足某人的需要
senses.example: The timetable was changed to accommodate working parents.
senses.exampleCN: 时间表被调整以照顾在职父母。
senses.why: Fitting a thing to a person becomes social courtesy: schedules and rules bend so that a need can be met.
senses.whyCN: 把事物合于人就变成社会性的体贴：时间表与规则弯一弯，以满足一项需要。

senses.title: To adapt oneself
senses.definition: to adjust one's behaviour or body to a new condition
senses.definitionCN: 调整行为或身体以适应新条件
senses.example: The eye accommodates to dim light within minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 眼睛在几分钟内适应昏暗光线。
senses.why: The reflexive form keeps the Latin core plainly: the see-er fits itself to what is seen.
senses.whyCN: 反身用法清楚保留拉丁核心：观看者使自己合于所见之物。

intro.en: Accommodate comes from Latin accommodare, 'to fit to', from ad- and commodus, 'fitting, suitable'.
intro.cn: accommodate 来自拉丁语 accommodare（使合于），由 ad- 与 commodus（合适的）构成。

items.en: modus meant 'measure', the root of mode and moderate.
items.cn: modus 意为「尺度」，是 mode 与 moderate 的词根。

items.en: commodus meant 'fitting, convenient', literally 'with due measure'.
items.cn: commodus 意为「合宜的、方便的」，字面是「合乎尺度」。

items.en: accommodare meant 'to fit one thing to another'.
items.cn: accommodare 意为「使一物合于另一物」。

items.en: accommodatio named the act of fitting or adjusting.
items.cn: accommodatio 指使之相合或调适的动作。

items.en: French accommoder extended the verb to lodging guests.
items.cn: 法语 accommoder 把动词扩展到安置客人。

items.en: English accommodate first meant to fit or suit, then to lodge.
items.cn: 英语 accommodate 先指使适合，后指提供住处。

note.en: The first group gathers the noun and the adjective; the second gathers verbs for holding and adjusting.
note.cn: 第一组收名词与形容词；第二组收表示容纳与调适的动词。

entries.definition: The noun for lodging or for an adjustment.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「住处」或「调适」。

entries.definition: An adjective for a helpful, flexible person.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「乐于助人的、通融的」。

entries.definition: A formal adjective meaning roomy and convenient.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，正式用法，义为「宽敞便利的」。

entries.definition: A verb meaning to contain or have capacity for.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「容纳」，有容量装下。

entries.definition: A verb meaning to provide a place for people or things.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「安置、收容」。

entries.definition: A verb meaning to change to suit conditions.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使适应」。

entries.definition: A phrasal verb meaning to provide for needs.
entries.definitionCN: 短语动词，义为「满足需要、提供所需」。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the Latin 'fit to' core and the capacity phrases; the abstract hooks picture chairs squeezed to make one more row.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用拉丁语「使合」核心与容量搭配；抽象记忆点想象椅子挤紧多出一排。

normal.en: Accommodate is 'fit to': Latin commodus means suitable.
normal.cn: accommodate 是「使合」：拉丁语 commodus 意为合适的。

normal.en: Accommodate guests and accommodate up to are the common patterns.
normal.cn: accommodate guests 与 accommodate up to 是常见结构。

normal.en: The noun is accommodation, with double m in both words.
normal.cn: 名词是 accommodation，两个词都双写 m。

normal.en: An accommodating person bends to help others.
normal.cn: an accommodating person 指愿意通融帮助别人的人。

normal.en: The verb covers rooms, capacity, needs, and the eye's adjustment.
normal.cn: 这个动词覆盖房间、容量、需求与眼睛的调适。

abstract.en: Picture chairs squeezed tighter so another row fits.
abstract.cn: 想象椅子挤紧以多放一排。

abstract.en: Picture a host moving furniture to make a bed for a guest.
abstract.cn: 想象主人挪家具给客人腾出床铺。

abstract.en: Picture an eye's pupil widening in a dim room.
abstract.cn: 想象昏暗房间里瞳孔放大。

examples.en: The hotel accommodates up to three hundred guests.
examples.cn: 这家旅馆最多可接待三百位客人。

examples.en: We rearranged the schedule to accommodate her treatment.
examples.cn: 我们重排日程以顾及她的治疗。

examples.en: Some animals accommodate quickly to changes in temperature.
examples.cn: 有些动物能迅速适应温度变化。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿科莫代特」——把东西挪一挪、合进去，就是容纳与照顾。

root: 拉丁语 ad-（向）+ modus（尺度）→ commodus（合宜的）→ accommodare（使合）；核心义是「把一方安置进另一方的尺度里」

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from giving someone a place, to measuring capacity, to bending arrangements for a need, to a body adjusting itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从给某人一个位置，走到测量容量，再到为需求调整安排，最后是身体自我调适。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: shifting things until one more fits in
core.cn: 核心意象：挪动物件直到多出一个位置

branches.en: A place found for a person to stay or sit.
branches.cn: 为某人找到住或坐的地方。

branches.en: A measured limit of how much fits.
branches.cn: 能容纳多少的量度上限。

branches.en: Arrangements bent to meet someone's need.
branches.cn: 为满足某人需求而调整的安排。

branches.en: A body fitting itself to new conditions.
branches.cn: 身体使自己适应新条件。

branches.en: Providing room and measuring room share the same fitting image.
branches.cn: 提供位置与测量容量共享同一个「合」的意象。

intro.en: The word joins the Latin prefix ad- with the measure root mod-, and its family adds the action noun and participle adjective.
intro.cn: 这个词把拉丁语前缀 ad- 与「尺度」词根 mod- 结合，词族另加动作名词与分词形容词。

latinIntro.en: Latin accommodare and accommodatio are the direct ancestors, so the Latin entries record the verb and its noun.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 accommodare 与 accommodatio 是直接祖先，因此拉丁条目记录动词与其名词。

derivatives.zh: 名词，义为「住处；调适」
形容词，义为「乐于助人的、通融的」

definition_zh: 住处；膳宿；调适；妥协；眼调节
definition_en: a place to live or stay, the act of adjusting to a need, an agreement between differing sides, or the eye's focusing adjustment
core_image: 把两张不同的尺寸量一量，凑成都能住下的安排
scene: 会议代表来自十几个国家，组委会提前订好酒店与合住的房间。The fee covers travel and accommodation.
sceneCN: 这里 accommodation 是「住处、膳宿」（第 1 个义项：供居住或停留的场所）；句意为费用包含交通与住宿。

derivatives.zh: 本词的动词形式，义为「容纳；提供住处」
由动词加现在分词后缀构成，义为「通融的」

senses.title: A place to stay
senses.definition: a room, building, or set of rooms where someone can live or stay
senses.definitionCN: 可供居住或停留的房间、建筑或套房
senses.example: The university guarantees accommodation for first-year students.
senses.exampleCN: 大学保证一年级学生的住宿。
senses.why: The -tion noun names the result of fitting people into a place, and that result is the building or room itself.
senses.whyCN: -tion 名词指把人安置进某处的结果，而这一结果就是房间或建筑本身。

senses.title: The act of adjusting to a need
senses.definition: the process of changing something so that it suits a condition
senses.definitionCN: 为适合某种条件而改变某物的过程
senses.example: The design shows careful accommodation to local climate.
senses.exampleCN: 该设计显示出对当地气候的细心顺应。
senses.why: Here the noun points back to the action: someone measures and bends a thing until it fits.
senses.whyCN: 这里名词回到动作本身：有人量一量、弯一弯，直到它合得上。

senses.title: A settlement between opposing sides
senses.definition: an arrangement in which conflicting parties each accept some of the other's position
senses.definitionCN: 冲突各方各自接受对方部分立场而形成的安排
senses.example: The two parties reached an accommodation over the disputed land.
senses.exampleCN: 两方就争议土地达成妥协。
senses.why: Social fitting is a bargain: each side gives a little so that both can fit inside one agreement.
senses.whyCN: 社会性的「合」是一场交易：各方让一点，才能同处一个协议之中。

senses.title: The eye's focusing adjustment
senses.definition: the change by which the eye's lens focuses on objects at different distances
senses.definitionCN: 眼睛晶状体对不同距离物体聚焦的变化
senses.example: Blurred reading in dim light can point to weak accommodation.
senses.exampleCN: 暗光下阅读模糊可能提示调节力不足。
senses.why: Physiology borrows the fitting image for the lens: it reshapes itself until the image fits the retina.
senses.whyCN: 生理学借这个「合」的意象描述晶状体：它改变形状，直到影像合于视网膜。

intro.en: Accommodation is the Latin action noun of accommodare, so it names both the act of fitting and the thing fitted.
intro.cn: accommodation 是 accommodare 的拉丁语动作名词，因此同时指「使合」的动作与被安置之物。

items.en: modus meant 'measure', the root behind mode.
items.cn: modus 意为「尺度」，是 mode 的词根。

items.en: commodus meant 'fitting, suitable'.
items.cn: commodus 意为「合宜的、合适的」。

items.en: accommodatio named the act of making something fit.
items.cn: accommodatio 指使某物相合的动作。

items.en: French accommodation covered lodging and adjustment alike.
items.cn: 法语 accommodation 兼指住宿与调适。

items.en: English accommodation first meant the act of fitting, then a place to stay.
items.cn: 英语 accommodation 先指使合的动作，后指居住之处。

items.en: Modern usage adds the settlement sense and the eye's focusing term.
items.cn: 现代用法增加了妥协义与眼睛调节的术语。

note.en: The first group gathers verb and adjective from the same family; the second gathers words for lodging and for agreement.
note.cn: 第一组收同族动词与形容词；第二组收表示住宿与协议的词。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to hold, lodge, or adjust.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「容纳、安置、适应」。

entries.definition: An adjective for someone willing to bend for others.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「通融的、乐于助人的」。

entries.definition: A formal adjective meaning spacious.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，正式用法，义为「宽敞的」。

entries.definition: A place to stay, often rented.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「寄宿处」，常为租住。

entries.definition: Buildings or arrangements for living in.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「住房」，供居住的建筑或安排。

entries.definition: An agreement in which each side gives up something.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「妥协」，各方各让一步的协议。

entries.definition: A small change made to fit a condition.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「调整」，为适合条件所做的小改变。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the -tion result pattern and the travel phrases; the abstract hooks picture two sizes measured until one arrangement fits both.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用 -tion 结果名词规律与旅行搭配；抽象记忆点想象两种尺寸量到同一安排都能容下。

normal.en: Accommodation is the -tion noun of accommodate, so it can mean the act or the place.
normal.cn: accommodation 是 accommodate 的 -tion 名词，可指动作或场所。

normal.en: In British English it is uncountable: student accommodation.
normal.cn: 英式英语中它不可数：student accommodation。

normal.en: Reach an accommodation means to settle a dispute.
normal.cn: reach an accommodation 意为解决争端。

normal.en: The verb keeps double m, and the noun keeps double m too.
normal.cn: 动词与名词都保留双写 m。

normal.en: In biology, accommodation is how the eye focuses.
normal.cn: 生物学中 accommodation 指眼睛的聚焦调节。

abstract.en: Picture a hotel desk booking rooms for a whole delegation.
abstract.cn: 想象旅馆前台为整个代表团订房。

abstract.en: Picture two negotiators each crossing out one demand.
abstract.cn: 想象两位谈判者各划掉一项要求。

abstract.en: Picture a lens thickening to bring a near page into focus.
abstract.cn: 想象晶状体变厚，把近处的书页聚焦清楚。

examples.en: Rent for accommodation near the campus has risen sharply.
examples.cn: 校园附近的住宿租金大幅上涨。

examples.en: The plan required accommodation to local rainfall patterns.
examples.cn: 该方案需要顺应当地降雨规律。

examples.en: The unions reached an accommodation on working hours.
examples.cn: 工会就工时达成妥协。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿科莫达申」——把人与地方量一量、合上，住处与妥协都是这个词。

root: 拉丁语 accommodatio（使相合）→ 法语 accommodation；核心义是「安置与调适的结果」

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from the place that results, to the act of adjusting, to a settlement between sides, to the eye's focusing.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从安置产生的地点，走到调适的动作，再到各方之间的妥协，最后是眼睛的聚焦调节。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two different measurements fitted into one arrangement
core.cn: 核心意象：两种不同尺寸被合进同一个安排

branches.en: The room or building that results from being fitted.
branches.cn: 安置之后产生的房间或建筑。

branches.en: The action of bending something to a condition.
branches.cn: 把某物弯向某条件的动作。

branches.en: An agreement that lets opposing sides coexist.
branches.cn: 让对立各方共处的协议。

branches.en: The lens reshaping until the image fits.
branches.cn: 晶状体改变形状直到影像合焦。

branches.en: A room and a deal are both arrangements people fit into.
branches.cn: 房间与协议都是人们嵌入其中的安排。

intro.en: The noun is the -tion form of the fitting verb, and its family keeps the verb and the participle adjective.
intro.cn: 这个名词是「使合」动词的 -tion 形式，词族保留动词与分词形容词。

latinIntro.en: Latin accommodatio is the direct ancestor, built from accommodare with the action suffix.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 accommodatio 是直接祖先，由 accommodare 加动作后缀构成。

形容词，义为「通融的」

definition_zh: 陪同；伴随；与……同时发生；为……伴奏
definition_en: to go with someone, to happen at the same time as something, or to play music for a performer
core_image: 一个人走在前，另一个人并肩跟着
scene: 老人去复查时不愿独自进诊室，女儿请了半天假陪着。Her daughter accompanied her to the clinic.
sceneCN: 这里 accompany 是「陪同」（第 1 个义项：与人同行）；句意为她女儿陪她去诊所。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「伴随物；伴奏」
由本词加表示人的后缀构成，义为「伴奏者」
由本词加现在分词后缀构成，义为「随附的」

senses.title: To go somewhere with someone
senses.definition: to travel or go with a person, especially to support or guard them
senses.definitionCN: 与人同行，尤指为支持或护送
senses.example: A nurse accompanies each patient into the theatre.
senses.exampleCN: 每位病人都有护士陪同进入手术室。
senses.why: Latin com- means 'with' and panis means 'bread'; to accompany was to share bread with a companion on the road.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 com- 意为「一起」，panis 意为「面包」；accompany 原指与同伴在旅途中分享面包。

senses.title: To happen together with
senses.definition: of an event or condition, to occur at the same time as something else
senses.definitionCN: 指事件或状况与另一事物同时出现
senses.example: Fever often accompanies the infection.
senses.exampleCN: 发热常伴随这种感染出现。
senses.why: Sharing a road becomes sharing a moment: whatever comes along at the same time is said to accompany the main event.
senses.whyCN: 共享一段路变成共享一个时刻：与主事件同时出现的一切，都称作伴随它。

senses.title: To play music for a performer
senses.definition: to play an instrument while someone sings or plays the main part
senses.definitionCN: 在他人演唱或演奏主旋律时演奏乐器
senses.example: A pianist accompanied the choir throughout the concert.
senses.exampleCN: 整场音乐会由一位钢琴家为合唱团伴奏。
senses.why: Music repeats the walking image: the accompaniment travels alongside the melody without taking the lead.
senses.whyCN: 音乐重复了同行意象：伴奏与主旋律同行，却不抢主导。

intro.en: Accompany comes from Old French acompaignier, 'to be a companion', from Latin com- 'with' and panis 'bread'.
intro.cn: accompany 来自古法语 acompaignier（作同伴），由拉丁语 com-（一起）与 panis（面包）构成。

items.en: panis meant 'bread', the source of pantry and pannier.
items.cn: panis 意为「面包」，是 pantry 与 pannier 的来源。

items.en: companio meant 'one who shares bread', a comrade.
items.cn: companio 意为「共享面包者」，即同伴。

items.en: compaign meant a companion or a group of comrades.
items.cn: compaign 指同伴或一伙伙伴。

items.en: acompaignier meant 'to join as a companion'.
items.cn: acompaignier 意为「作为同伴加入」。

items.en: English accompany first meant to travel with a companion.
items.cn: 英语 accompany 最初指与同伴同行。

items.en: Modern usage adds simultaneous events and musical accompaniment.
items.cn: 现代用法增加了同时发生的事件与音乐伴奏。

note.en: The first group gathers the noun, the player word, and the participle; the second gathers verbs for going along with.
note.cn: 第一组收名词、伴奏者与分词；第二组收表示同行的动词。

entries.definition: Something that goes with another thing, including music.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「伴随物；伴奏」。

entries.definition: A person who plays music to support a performer.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「伴奏者」。

entries.definition: A person who shares a journey or daily life.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「同伴」，共享旅途或日常生活的人。

entries.definition: A verb meaning to go with someone for protection or guidance.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「护送、陪同」。

entries.definition: A verb meaning to go with or be present at.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「伴随、出席」。

entries.definition: A verb meaning to happen at the same time.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「同时发生」。

entries.definition: A verb meaning to support a performer with music.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「为……伴奏」。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the 'share bread' origin and the clinic phrases; the abstract hooks picture two figures walking side by side.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用「分面包」来源与诊所搭配；抽象记忆点想象两个并肩前行的身影。

normal.en: Accompany is 'share bread': com- with, panis bread.
normal.cn: accompany 是「共享面包」：com- 一起，panis 面包。

normal.en: Be accompanied by is the passive pattern in news reports.
normal.cn: be accompanied by 是新闻报道中的被动结构。

normal.en: Accompanying symptoms are signs that come with an illness.
normal.cn: accompanying symptoms 指与疾病同时出现的症状。

normal.en: A pianist accompanies a singer; the noun is accompaniment.
normal.cn: 钢琴家为歌手伴奏；名词是 accompaniment。

normal.en: The verb doubles no letters but changes y to i before -ed.
normal.cn: 这个动词不双写字母，但加 -ed 时把 y 变 i。

abstract.en: Picture two figures walking side by side on a road.
abstract.cn: 想象两个身影在路上并肩行走。

abstract.en: Picture a cough that arrives with a fever.
abstract.cn: 想象咳嗽伴随发热而来。

abstract.en: Picture piano notes following a melody without leading it.
abstract.cn: 想象钢琴音符跟随旋律而不主导。

examples.en: Children must be accompanied by an adult.
examples.cn: 儿童必须由成人陪同。

examples.en: Strong winds accompanied the storm.
examples.cn: 强风伴随这场暴风雨而来。

examples.en: He accompanied her on the violin.
examples.cn: 他用小提琴为她伴奏。

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from walking with a person, to events occurring together, to music travelling alongside a melody.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从与人同行，走到事件同时发生，再到音乐与主旋律同行。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two people sharing one road
core.cn: 核心意象：两人共享同一条路

branches.en: A person going with another to a place.
branches.cn: 与另一人同往某地者。

branches.en: An event or condition arriving with another.
branches.cn: 与另一事件同来的状况。

branches.en: Music that follows a main performer.
branches.cn: 跟随主表演者的音乐。

branches.en: A companion and an accompanist both travel alongside.
branches.cn: 同伴与伴奏者都在一旁同行。

branches.en: Simultaneous events are companions in time.
branches.cn: 同时发生的事件是时间上的同伴。

intro.en: The word joins the Latin 'with' prefix com- with the bread root pan-, and its family adds noun and person endings.
intro.cn: 这个词把拉丁语前缀 com-（一起）与「面包」词根 pan- 结合，词族另加名词与人物后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin companio is the ancestor behind companion and the verb, so the Latin entries record the noun and its derived verb.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 companio 是 companion 与该动词背后的祖先，因此拉丁条目记录名词与其派生动词。

derivatives.zh: 名词，义为「伴随物；伴奏」
名词，义为「伴奏者」

definition_zh: 共犯；帮凶；同伙
definition_en: a person who helps another person commit a crime
core_image: 一个人动手，另一个人在门口望风
scene: 监控里看到，进店偷东西的只有一人，但门外有人不断打手势提醒时间。Police later arrested his accomplice.
sceneCN: 这里 accomplice 是「共犯、帮凶」（第 1 个义项：协助他人犯罪者）；句意为警方后来逮捕了他的同伙。

derivatives.zh: 同源动词，义为「陪同」，语义上指同行之人

senses.title: A helper in a crime
senses.definition: a person who knowingly helps another to commit an offence
senses.definitionCN: 明知而协助他人实施犯罪的人
senses.example: The driver was charged as an accomplice in the escape.
senses.exampleCN: 司机作为逃跑帮凶被起诉。
senses.why: The word grew from complice, 'one joined with another'; in law that joining is a partnership in wrongdoing.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由 complice（与他人联结者）演变而来；法律上这种联结就是共同作恶的伙伴关系。

senses.title: A partner in mischief
senses.definition: a person who joins another in a mischievous or foolish act, without legal seriousness
senses.definitionCN: 与他人一起做淘气或愚蠢之事者，不含法律严重性
senses.example: Her little brother was her accomplice in hiding the cake.
senses.exampleCN: 她弟弟是她藏蛋糕的同伙。
senses.why: Outside law, the word's 'partner' frame survives in jokes: the partner shares the scheme, if not the crime.
senses.whyCN: 在法律之外，这个词的「伙伴」框架残存在玩笑中：伙伴分担的是主意，未必是罪。

intro.en: Accomplice comes from Old French complice, reshaped by association with accomplish; both trace to Latin complere, 'to fill up'.
intro.cn: accomplice 来自古法语 complice，因与 accomplish 联想而被改写；二者都可追到拉丁语 complere（填满）。

items.en: complere meant 'to fill up, complete', from com- and plere 'to fill'.
items.cn: complere 意为「填满、完成」，由 com- 与 plere（填）构成。

items.en: complex meant 'woven together, closely connected'.
items.cn: complex 意为「交织在一起、紧密关联的」。

items.en: complice meant an associate or partner in a matter.
items.cn: complice 指某事中的同伙或伙伴。

items.en: English borrowed complice, then inserted an a by confusion with accomplish.
items.cn: 英语借入 complice，后因与 accomplish 混淆而插入 a。

items.en: Criminal law fixed accomplice for a person who aids an offence.
items.cn: 刑法固定 accomplice 指协助犯罪者。

items.en: Modern usage keeps the legal sense and a lighter playful one.
items.cn: 现代用法保留法律义与较轻的戏谑义。

note.en: The first group gathers look-alikes often confused with it; the second gathers words for a partner in wrongdoing.
note.cn: 第一组收易混的近形词；第二组收表示共同作恶者的词。

entries.definition: A verb meaning to complete a task successfully.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「完成、实现」。

entries.definition: An adjective for a highly skilled person.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「技艺高超的」。

entries.definition: A verb meaning to go with someone.

entries.definition: An adjective meaning obedient to rules.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「顺从的、合规的」。

entries.definition: A general word for a person working with another.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「伙伴」，泛指与他人合作者。

entries.definition: A legal term for a person who assists a crime.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，法律用语，义为「从犯」。

entries.definition: A person joined with others in a plot.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「同谋者」，参与密谋者。

entries.definition: A loyal follower who carries out another's plans.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「亲信、打手」，执行他人计划者。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the inserted-a story and the police phrases; the abstract hooks picture one thief inside and one watcher outside.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用「插入 a」的拼写故事与警务搭配；抽象记忆点想象一人店内行窃、一人在外望风。

normal.en: Accomplice looks like accomplish, but it means a partner in crime.
normal.cn: accomplice 看起来像 accomplish，却指犯罪同伙。

normal.en: The a was inserted by confusion with accomplish.
normal.cn: 那个 a 是因与 accomplish 混淆而插入的。

normal.en: An accomplice to the crime is the standard legal phrase.
normal.cn: an accomplice to the crime 是标准法律短语。

normal.en: The plural is accomplices, keeping the c soft.
normal.cn: 复数是 accomplices，c 仍读软音。

normal.en: In law, accomplice and accessory are distinct roles.
normal.cn: 法律上 accomplice 与 accessory 是不同角色。

abstract.en: Picture one person inside a shop and one watching the street.
abstract.cn: 想象一人在店内、一人在街上望风。

abstract.en: Picture two children hiding a cake in a cupboard.
abstract.cn: 想象两个孩子把蛋糕藏进橱柜。

abstract.en: Picture a driver waiting with the engine running.
abstract.cn: 想象一辆车开着引擎等待。

examples.en: She was convicted as an accomplice in the fraud.
examples.cn: 她作为诈骗案共犯被定罪。

examples.en: The robber's accomplice waited in the car.
examples.cn: 劫匪的同伙在车里等候。

examples.en: His accomplice in the prank was the quietest boy in class.
examples.cn: 他搞恶作剧的同伙是班上最安静的男孩。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿康普利斯」——一个人动手，另一个人在门口打手势，就是帮凶。

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from the legal partner in a crime, to the lighter partner in mischief.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从法律上的犯罪同伙，走到较轻的恶作剧同伙。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one person acts while another stands watch
core.cn: 核心意象：一人行动，另一人望风

branches.en: A person who knowingly aids an offence.
branches.cn: 明知而协助犯罪者。

branches.en: A partner in a harmless prank.
branches.cn: 无害恶作剧中的伙伴。

branches.en: Both senses rest on a shared scheme.
branches.cn: 两个义项都建立在共同的谋划上。

branches.en: The legal word and the playful word are one frame with different weights.
branches.cn: 法律词与戏谑词是同一框架的不同分量。

branches.en: A partner's role ranges from watching to sharing the blame.
branches.cn: 伙伴的角色从望风到分担罪责。

intro.en: The word keeps a Latin 'together' prefix and a filling root, with the -ice ending marking a person.
intro.cn: 这个词保留拉丁语「一起」前缀与「填」词根，并以 -ice 后缀指人。

latinIntro.en: Latin complex and the French form complice are the ancestors, so the Latin entries record the root and the derived adjective.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 complex 与法语形式 complice 是祖先，因此拉丁条目记录词根与派生形容词。

名词，义为「同谋、串通」

definition_zh: 完成；实现；达到
definition_en: to succeed in doing or completing something planned
core_image: 清单上最后一项被划掉，笔尖停住
scene: 他花了三个月修补旧钟，最后一个齿轮咬合时，秒针重新走了起来。They accomplished the repair without new parts.
sceneCN: 这里 accomplish 是「完成」（第 1 个义项：把计划中的事做完）；句意为他们没有用新零件就完成了修理。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「成就；完成」
由本词加过去分词后缀构成，义为「技艺高超的」

senses.title: To complete a task
senses.definition: to carry out a piece of work until it is finished
senses.definitionCN: 把一项工作做到结束
senses.example: The team accomplished the survey in two weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 团队用两周完成了这次调查。
senses.why: Latin complere meant 'to fill up'; accomplish adds ad- and keeps the image of filling a task until nothing is missing.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 complere 意为「填满」；accomplish 加上 ad-，保留「把任务填满、不留缺口」的意象。

senses.title: To achieve an aim
senses.definition: to succeed in reaching something intended or desired
senses.definitionCN: 成功达到意图或期望之物
senses.example: They accomplished more than anyone expected.
senses.exampleCN: 他们取得的成果超出所有人的预期。
senses.why: The filled measure can be a goal rather than a task: the aim is reached and nothing remains to be done.
senses.whyCN: 被填满的尺度也可以是目标而非任务：目的达到，再无未竟之事。

senses.title: To bring to full development
senses.definition: in older use, to complete a person's training or a design's quality
senses.definitionCN: 旧用法中，完成一个人的训练或使设计达到完善
senses.example: Years of practice accomplished him as a violinist.
senses.exampleCN: 多年练习把他造就成一名小提琴手。
senses.why: This older sense survives mainly in the adjective accomplished, where completion means polished skill.
senses.whyCN: 这一旧义主要残存在形容词 accomplished 中，那里的「完成」意味着娴熟的技艺。

intro.en: Accomplish comes from Old French acomplir, from Latin complere, 'to fill up'.
intro.cn: accomplish 来自古法语 acomplir，源自拉丁语 complere（填满）。

items.en: plere meant 'to fill', the root of complete and supplement.
items.cn: plere 意为「填」，是 complete 与 supplement 的词根。

items.en: complere meant 'to fill up, finish'.
items.cn: complere 意为「填满、完成」。

items.en: acomplir meant 'to fulfil, carry out'.
items.cn: acomplir 意为「履行、完成」。

items.en: English accomplish first meant to complete a duty or a period.
items.cn: 英语 accomplish 最初指完成职责或一段时间。

items.en: The participle accomplished came to mean highly skilled.
items.cn: 分词 accomplished 逐渐表示技艺高超。

items.en: Modern usage concentrates on tasks and goals.
items.cn: 现代用法集中在任务与目标。

note.en: The first group gathers the noun and the participle adjective; the second gathers verbs of finishing.
note.cn: 第一组收名词与分词形容词；第二组收表示完成的动词。

entries.definition: The noun for an achievement or the act of finishing.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「成就」或「完成的行为」。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning highly skilled.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「技艺高超的」。

entries.definition: A partner in a crime, often confused with this word.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「共犯」，常与本词混淆。

entries.definition: An adjective and verb from the same Latin filling root.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词与动词，同出拉丁语「填满」词根。

entries.definition: A verb meaning to reach a goal through effort.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「实现、达到」，经努力达到目标。

entries.definition: A verb meaning to carry out a promise or need.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「履行、满足」。

entries.definition: A verb meaning to finish something begun.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「完成」，结束已开始之事。

entries.definition: A phrasal verb meaning to perform a plan or order.
entries.definitionCN: 短语动词，义为「执行、实施」。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the 'fill up' root and the task phrases; the abstract hooks picture the last box on a list being ticked.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用「填满」词根与任务搭配；抽象记忆点想象清单最后一格被划掉。

normal.en: Accomplish is Latin 'fill up': complere means to fill.
normal.cn: accomplish 是拉丁语「填满」：complere 意为填。

normal.en: Accomplish a task and accomplish a goal are the two patterns.
normal.cn: accomplish a task 与 accomplish a goal 是两种搭配。

normal.en: The noun is accomplishment, the participle accomplished.
normal.cn: 名词是 accomplishment，分词是 accomplished。

normal.en: Accomplished describes a skilled musician or writer.
normal.cn: accomplished 形容技艺高超的音乐家或作家。

normal.en: Watch the ending: -ish, not -ice like accomplice.
normal.cn: 注意词尾：是 -ish，而不是 accomplice 的 -ice。

abstract.en: Picture the last box on a long checklist being ticked.
abstract.cn: 想象一长串清单上最后一格被划掉。

abstract.en: Picture a clock's last gear clicking into place.
abstract.cn: 想象钟表最后一个齿轮咔哒咬合。

abstract.en: Picture a goalpost reached after a long uphill run.
abstract.cn: 想象长坡跑后抵达球门柱。

examples.en: The crew accomplished the rescue in darkness.
examples.cn: 救援队摸黑完成了救援。

examples.en: Little was accomplished by the second meeting.
examples.cn: 第二次会议几乎没取得任何成果。

examples.en: She is an accomplished cellist as well as a doctor.
examples.cn: 她既是医生，也是一位技艺高超的大提琴手。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿康普利什」——把一项任务填满、填到没有缺口，就是完成。

sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从把一件工作做完，走到达到目的，再到旧有的「使人技艺完善」义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the last item on a checklist crossed out

branches.en: A piece of work carried to its end.
branches.cn: 被做到尽头的一项工作。

branches.en: An intended aim actually reached.
branches.cn: 真正达到的预期目的。

branches.en: A person brought to polished skill.
branches.cn: 被造就到技艺娴熟的人。

branches.en: Task and goal are two kinds of full measure.
branches.cn: 任务与目标是两种「填满」的尺度。

branches.en: Reaching a goal and perfecting a craft both end in accomplishment.
branches.cn: 达到目标与完善技艺都以成就收尾。

intro.en: The word joins the Latin prefix ad- with the filling root pl-, and its family adds the action noun and participle.
intro.cn: 这个词把拉丁语前缀 ad- 与「填」词根 pl- 结合，词族另加动作名词与分词。

latinIntro.en: Latin complere is the direct ancestor, so the Latin entries record the verb and its participle.

definition_zh: 成就；完成；才艺；修养
definition_en: something successfully done, the act of finishing it, or a skill gained through training
core_image: 墙上挂着一张完成证书，旁边还摆着练习多年的乐器
scene: 老人把年轻时的奖状、修好的收音机和自学的吉他照片一起摆在书架上。Her chief accomplishment was teaching herself three languages.
sceneCN: 这里 accomplishment 是「成就」（第 1 个义项：成功做成的事）；句意为她最大的成就是自学了三门语言。

derivatives.zh: 本词的动词形式，义为「完成；实现」
由动词加过去分词后缀构成，义为「技艺高超的」

senses.title: Something successfully achieved
senses.definition: a result that has been achieved through effort and skill
senses.definitionCN: 经努力与技能取得的结果
senses.example: Finishing the marathon was her greatest accomplishment.
senses.exampleCN: 跑完马拉松是她最大的成就。
senses.why: The -ment ending marks a result, so accomplishment is the completed thing standing in view after the effort ends.
senses.whyCN: -ment 后缀标记结果，因此 accomplishment 是努力结束后摆在眼前的已完成之物。

senses.title: The act of completing something
senses.definition: the carrying out or finishing of a task, duty, or plan
senses.definitionCN: 任务、职责或计划的执行完毕
senses.example: The accomplishment of the treaty took another year.
senses.exampleCN: 条约的完成又花了一年。
senses.why: Here the noun names the process rather than the trophy: the filling up of a task, step by step.
senses.whyCN: 这里名词指过程而非奖杯：一项任务被一步步填满。

senses.title: A learned skill or grace
senses.definition: a ability polished by training, often social or artistic
senses.definitionCN: 经训练打磨的能力，常指社交或艺术方面
senses.example: Her accomplishments included watercolour painting and fluent Italian.
senses.exampleCN: 她的才艺包括水彩画和流利的意大利语。
senses.why: In older polite society, a person's accomplishments were the skills that completed a good education.
senses.whyCN: 在旧时上流社会，一个人的 accomplishments 是使良好教育「完整」的那些技艺。

intro.en: Accomplishment adds the result suffix -ment to the verb accomplish, so it names what a completed effort leaves behind.
intro.cn: accomplishment 在动词 accomplish 上加结果后缀 -ment，指完成努力后留下的东西。

items.en: plere meant 'to fill', the root of complete.

items.en: acomplir meant 'to fulfil or carry out'.
items.cn: acomplir 意为「履行、完成」。

items.cn: 英语先构成动词，再加 -ment 构成名词。

items.cn: 复数 accomplishments 在十七世纪指教育中的文雅技艺。

items.cn: 现代用法强调成就与成就感。

note.cn: 第一组收动词与其分词；第二组收表示成就与技艺的词。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to complete or achieve.

entries.definition: An adjective for a skilled performer or writer.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「技艺高超的」。

entries.definition: A partner in crime, a common spelling trap.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「共犯」，常见拼写陷阱。

entries.definition: Something important done through effort.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「成就」，经努力做成的重要之事。

entries.definition: An impressive act requiring skill or courage.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「壮举」，需要技艺或勇气。

entries.definition: An ability learned through practice.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「技能」，经练习获得的能力。

entries.definition: The reaching of a goal or a gained ability.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「达到；造诣」。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the -ment result rule and the award phrases; the abstract hooks picture a certificate beside a well-used instrument.

normal.en: Accomplishment is accomplish plus -ment, so it is the result.
normal.cn: accomplishment 是 accomplish 加 -ment，指结果。

normal.en: A sense of accomplishment is the everyday phrase for pride after effort.
normal.cn: a sense of accomplishment 是努力后自豪感的日常说法。

normal.en: The plural often means polite skills: her accomplishments.
normal.cn: 复数常指文雅技艺：her accomplishments。

normal.en: Use accomplishment for the thing done, the accomplishment of for the act.
normal.cn: 指做成之事用 accomplishment，指完成的行为用 the accomplishment of。

normal.en: The spelling has double c but a single m: a-c-c-o-m-p-l-i-s-h.
normal.cn: 拼写是双 c、单 m：a-c-c-o-m-p-l-i-s-h。

abstract.en: Picture a framed certificate above a scratched guitar.
abstract.cn: 想象镶框证书上方挂着一把划痕斑驳的吉他。

abstract.en: Picture a runner crossing a line and checking the watch.
abstract.cn: 想象跑者越过终点线看表。

abstract.en: Picture a treaty signed after a year of small steps.
abstract.cn: 想象一年小步推进后签署的条约。

examples.en: Learning to swim was a real accomplishment for him.
examples.cn: 学会游泳对他而言是真正的成就。

examples.en: The accomplishment of the bridge took four years.
examples.cn: 这座桥的建成花了四年。

examples.en: Her accomplishments include piano and fluent German.
examples.cn: 她的才艺包括钢琴和流利的德语。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿康普利什门特」——努力结束后摆在眼前的那个成果，就是成就。

root: accomplish（完成）+ -ment（结果）；核心义是「把任务填满后留下的成果」

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from the finished result, to the act of finishing, to the skills that complete an education.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从完成后的结果，走到完成的行为，再到使教育「完整」的技艺。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a certificate hung beside a much-used instrument
core.cn: 核心意象：挂在用旧乐器旁的证书

branches.en: The achieved result that can be pointed to.
branches.cn: 可以指认的完成结果。

branches.en: The process of carrying a duty to its end.
branches.cn: 把职责做到尽头的过程。

branches.en: A trained ability that rounds out a person.
branches.cn: 使一个人更完整的受训能力。

branches.en: The trophy and the process share one noun.
branches.cn: 成果与过程共用同一个名词。

branches.en: A skill can itself be the achievement.
branches.cn: 技艺本身就可以是成就。

intro.en: The noun is the -ment result form of the filling verb, and its family keeps the verb and participle.
intro.cn: 这个名词是「填满」动词的 -ment 结果形式，词族保留动词与分词。

latinIntro.en: Latin complere is the ancestor behind the verb, and -ment reached English through French.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 complere 是该动词背后的祖先，-ment 经法语进入英语。

derivatives.zh: 动词，义为「完成；实现」
形容词，义为「技艺高超的」

definition_zh: 协议；一致；给予；与……相符
definition_en: an agreement, a state of matching, to give something formally, or to be consistent with
core_image: 两颗心朝同一个方向，拍子落在同一拍上
scene: 两国代表在桌边交换文本，随后握手，条款与各自的承诺完全吻合。The two sides signed an accord on fishing rights.
sceneCN: 这里 accord 是「协议」（第 1 个义项：正式达成的约定）；句意为双方签署了一项渔业权协议。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「一致、符合」，见于 in accordance with
由 accordance 加副词后缀构成，义为「相应地、因此」
形近名词，义为「手风琴」

senses.title: A formal agreement
senses.definition: an official arrangement accepted by two or more parties
senses.definitionCN: 两方或多方接受的正式安排
senses.example: The trade accord lowered tariffs on both sides.
senses.exampleCN: 这项贸易协定降低了两边的关税。
senses.why: Latin ad- 'to' plus cor 'heart' gave accordare, 'to bring hearts together'; an agreement is a meeting of wills.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 ad-（向）加 cor（心）构成 accordare（使心相合）；协议就是意志的相遇。

senses.title: A state of agreement
senses.definition: the condition of matching or being of one mind
senses.definitionCN: 彼此相符或意见相同的状态
senses.example: They acted of one accord when the alarm sounded.
senses.exampleCN: 警报响起时，他们一致行动。
senses.why: Before it named documents, accord named the harmony itself, and the old phrase of one accord still preserves that.
senses.whyCN: 在指文件之前，accord 指和谐状态本身，古语 of one accord 仍保留这一层。

senses.title: To give something formally
senses.definition: to grant a right, honour, or treatment to someone
senses.definitionCN: 给予某人权利、荣誉或待遇
senses.example: The court accorded her the right to appeal.
senses.exampleCN: 法院给予她上诉权。
senses.why: Granting a privilege is putting two wills into accord: the giver and the receiver agree on what is handed over.
senses.whyCN: 授予特权就是把两种意志调成一致：给予者与接受者就所转交之物达成一致。

senses.title: To be consistent with
senses.definition: to match or agree with a fact, rule, or account
senses.definitionCN: 与事实、规则或说法相符
senses.example: His account does not accord with the physical evidence.
senses.exampleCN: 他的说法与物证不符。
senses.why: Things, not just people, can be in accord: a story and a fact line up like two notes on the same beat.
senses.whyCN: 不只是人可以一致，事物也可以：说法与事实像同一拍上的两个音对齐。

intro.en: Accord comes from Latin accordare, 'to bring hearts together', from ad- and cor, 'heart'.
intro.cn: accord 来自拉丁语 accordare（使心相合），由 ad- 与 cor（心）构成。

items.en: cor meant 'heart', the root of cordial and record.
items.cn: cor 意为「心」，是 cordial 与 record 的词根。

items.en: The prefix ad- meant 'to, toward'.
items.cn: 前缀 ad- 意为「向」。

items.en: accordare meant 'to bring to one heart, reconcile'.
items.cn: accordare 意为「使同心、调和」。

items.en: acord meant agreement or harmony.
items.cn: acord 意为「一致、和谐」。

items.en: English accord first meant harmony, then a formal agreement.
items.cn: 英语 accord 先指和谐，后指正式协议。

items.en: Modern usage keeps the verb for granting and for matching facts.
items.cn: 现代用法保留动词的「授予」与「相符」义。

note.en: The first group gathers the noun and adverb of the same family plus the musical look-alike; the second gathers words for agreements.
note.cn: 第一组收同族名词、副词与形近的音乐词；第二组收表示协议与一致的词。

entries.definition: A noun used in the phrase in accordance with.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，见于短语 in accordance with（依照）。

entries.definition: An adverb meaning 'therefore' or 'in a matching way'.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「因此」或「相应地」。

entries.definition: A musical instrument with a folding keyboard.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「手风琴」，带可折叠键盘的乐器。

entries.definition: A written account, from the same Latin heart root.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「记录」，同出拉丁语「心」词根。

entries.definition: A general word for a shared decision.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「协议、一致」，泛指共同决定。

entries.definition: A formal agreement between states.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「条约」，国家间的正式协议。

entries.definition: A state of peaceful agreement.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「和谐」，和平一致的状态。

entries.definition: A verb meaning to give a right or favour.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「授予」，给予权利或恩惠。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the 'one heart' image and the treaty phrases; the abstract hooks picture two hands clapping on the same beat.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用「同心」意象与条约搭配；抽象记忆点想象两只手落在同一拍上。

normal.en: Accord is Latin 'heart together': cor means heart.
normal.cn: accord 是拉丁语「同心」：cor 意为心。

normal.en: Peace accord and trade accord are the news phrases.
normal.cn: peace accord 与 trade accord 是新闻用语。

normal.en: In accord with and accord with both express matching.
normal.cn: in accord with 与 accord with 都表示相符。

normal.en: Of one accord is a fixed phrase for unanimous action.
normal.cn: of one accord 是表示一致行动的固定短语。

normal.en: The everyday relatives are accordance and accordingly.
normal.cn: 日常同族词是 accordance 与 accordingly。

abstract.en: Picture two delegates signing the same page at one table.
abstract.cn: 想象两位代表在同一桌前签署同一页。

abstract.en: Picture two hands clapping on exactly the same beat.
abstract.cn: 想象两只手落在完全同一拍上。

abstract.en: Picture a judge handing a sealed paper across the bench.
abstract.cn: 想象法官隔着法台递出一份盖章文件。

examples.en: The peace accord was signed after months of talks.
examples.cn: 和平协议在数月谈判后签署。

examples.en: The findings do not accord with the earlier report.
examples.cn: 这些发现与早先的报告不符。

examples.en: The best students were accorded special funding.
examples.cn: 最优秀的学生被给予特别资助。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿科德」——两颗心朝同一个方向，就是一致与协议。

root: 拉丁语 ad-（向）+ cor（心）→ accordare（使同心）；核心义是「意志或事实落在同一拍上」

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from the signed document, to the harmony behind it, to the act of granting, to facts that match.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从签署的文件，走到其背后的和谐，再到授予的动作，最后是彼此相合的事实。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two hearts beating on the same beat
core.cn: 核心意象：两颗心在同一拍上跳动

branches.en: An official arrangement signed by parties.
branches.cn: 各方签署的正式安排。

branches.en: The harmony that the document records.
branches.cn: 文件所记录的和谐状态。

branches.en: A right or honour handed to someone.
branches.cn: 交给某人的权利或荣誉。

branches.en: A statement that lines up with the evidence.
branches.cn: 与证据对得上的说法。

branches.en: The paper and the harmony are the same idea at two stages.
branches.cn: 文件与和谐是同一观念的两个阶段。

intro.en: The word joins the Latin prefix ad- with the heart root cord-, and its family adds noun and adverb forms.
intro.cn: 这个词把拉丁语前缀 ad- 与「心」词根 cord- 结合，词族另加名词与副词形式。

latinIntro.en: Latin accordare is the direct ancestor, built on cor, so the Latin entries record the heart noun and the verb.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 accordare 是直接祖先，由 cor 构成，因此拉丁条目记录「心」名词与动词。

derivatives.zh: 名词，义为「一致、符合」
副词，义为「相应地、因此」

definition_zh: 手风琴；可折叠的
definition_en: a musical instrument with a folding bellows and keyboard, or a pleated folding style
core_image: 一叠风箱被拉开又合上，挤出一个个音
scene: 街角艺人把琴抱在胸前，一拉一合，风箱像手风琴一样伸展。He played an accordion on the corner every evening.
sceneCN: 这里 accordion 是「手风琴」（第 1 个义项：带折叠风箱的键盘乐器）；句意为他每天傍晚在街角拉手风琴。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加表示人的后缀构成，义为「手风琴演奏者」
形近名词，义为「协议」

senses.title: A folding musical instrument
senses.definition: a portable instrument with a bellows and keys that produces sound when squeezed
senses.definitionCN: 带风箱与键、挤压发声的便携乐器
senses.example: She learned the accordion from her grandfather.
senses.exampleCN: 她跟祖父学拉手风琴。
senses.why: The name came from German Akkordion, a coined word for an instrument whose parts are in accord, or harmony.
senses.whyCN: 这一名称来自德语 Akkordion，是为这种「各部件相和」的乐器造的词。

senses.title: A pleated or folding form
senses.definition: of a file, door, or sheet, folding in and out like a bellows
senses.definitionCN: 指文件夹、门或纸张像风箱一样来回折叠
senses.example: She keeps receipts in an accordion folder by month.
senses.exampleCN: 她按月把收据放在风琴式文件夹里。
senses.why: Because the bellows folds in deep pleats, everyday objects that fold the same way borrow the instrument's name.
senses.whyCN: 由于风箱折成深褶，以同样方式折叠的日常物件便借用了这件乐器的名字。

intro.en: Accordion is a nineteenth-century coinage from German Akkordion, built on Accord, 'harmony'.
intro.cn: accordion 是十九世纪由德语 Akkordion 造出的词，建立在 Accord（和谐）之上。

items.en: cor meant 'heart', the root behind accord.
items.cn: cor 意为「心」，是 accord 背后的词根。

items.en: accordare meant 'to bring into harmony'.
items.cn: accordare 意为「使和谐」。

items.en: Akkord meant a chord or a harmonious combination of notes.
items.cn: Akkord 意为和弦或和谐的音组合。

items.en: The name was coined for an instrument combining reed pipes and bellows.
items.cn: 这一名称是为结合簧管与风箱的乐器而造。

items.en: English borrowed accordion as the instrument spread across Europe.
items.cn: 随着乐器传遍欧洲，英语借入 accordion。

items.en: Modern usage adds the pleated-file and folding-door senses.
items.cn: 现代用法增加了风琴式文件夹与折叠门义。

note.en: The first group gathers the player word, the root noun, and the look-alike; the second gathers words for the instrument and for folding.
note.cn: 第一组收演奏者、同源名词与形近词；第二组收表示乐器与折叠的词。

entries.definition: A person who plays the accordion.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「手风琴演奏者」。

entries.definition: An agreement or harmony, the word behind the name.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「协议、和谐」，名称所本之词。

entries.definition: A folder with pleated pockets.
entries.definitionCN: 名词短语，义为「风琴式文件夹」。

entries.definition: A similar squeezebox instrument with a different mechanism.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「六角手风琴」，机理不同的同类乐器。

entries.definition: A small mouth organ, also built on a harmony word.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「口琴」，名称同样出自「和谐」。

entries.definition: An adjective for fabric folded into regular ridges.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有褶的」。

entries.definition: An adjective for something made to fold up.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「可折叠的」。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the harmony name and the street-musician scene; the abstract hooks picture a bellows opening and closing in pleats.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用「和谐」名称与街头艺人场景；抽象记忆点想象风箱一开一合的褶皱。

normal.en: Accordion is built on accord, 'harmony': notes and parts that agree.
normal.cn: accordion 建立在 accord（和谐）之上：相互协调的音与部件。

normal.en: Play the accordion uses the definite article in English.
normal.cn: play the accordion 在英语中要加定冠词。

normal.en: An accordion file folds in and out like bellows.
normal.cn: an accordion file 像风箱一样折叠。

normal.en: The player is an accordionist.
normal.cn: 演奏者是 accordionist。

normal.en: Do not confuse it with accord, the agreement word.
normal.cn: 不要与表示协议的 accord 混淆。

abstract.en: Picture a street musician squeezing a bellows against his chest.
abstract.cn: 想象街头艺人把风箱抱在胸前挤压。

abstract.en: Picture a file with pockets that spread open like stairs.
abstract.cn: 想象文件夹的袋口像台阶一样张开。

abstract.en: Picture a folding door narrowing the room in pleats.
abstract.cn: 想象折叠门以褶皱把房间收窄。

examples.en: The band includes a fiddler and an accordion player.
examples.cn: 乐队里有一位小提琴手和一位手风琴手。

examples.en: He filed the invoices in an accordion folder.
examples.cn: 他把发票放进风琴式文件夹。

examples.en: The accordion door saves space in the narrow hall.
examples.cn: 折叠门为狭窄走廊节省空间。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿科迪昂」——一叠风箱拉开来全是褶，合起来就成调。

root: 德语 Akkordion，源自 Accord（和谐）；核心义是「以折叠风箱挤出和谐音的乐器」

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from the instrument itself, to anything folded in the same pleated way.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从乐器本身，走到任何以同样褶皱方式折叠的物件。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bellows opening into pleats and closing into a note
core.cn: 核心意象：风箱张开成褶、合拢成音

branches.en: The squeezebox instrument with keys and bellows.
branches.cn: 带键与风箱的便携乐器。

branches.en: A file or door that folds like a bellows.
branches.cn: 像风箱一样折叠的文件夹或门。

branches.en: The instrument's shape gives the folding objects their name.
branches.cn: 乐器的形状给了折叠物件名称。

branches.en: The deep pleats are the shared picture.
branches.cn: 深褶皱是共享的图景。

branches.en: One word covers a sound and a silhouette.
branches.cn: 同一个词覆盖一种声音与一种轮廓。

intro.en: The word joins the harmony noun with a Greek-style ending, and its family adds the player suffix and the related accord words.
intro.cn: 这个词把「和谐」名词与希腊式词尾结合，词族另加演奏者后缀与相关 accord 词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin heart noun cor stands behind accord and thus behind accordion, so those entries are recorded.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语「心」名词 cor 在 accord 之后，也就在 accordion 之后，因此收录这些条目。

definition_zh: 上前搭话；拦住（陌生人）；乞讨纠缠
definition_en: to approach and speak to someone, especially in a bold or unwanted way
core_image: 一个人从路边横跨一步，挡在行人面前开口
scene: 游客刚出车站，就有人贴上来问要不要换钱，一路跟着走了半条街。A stranger accosted him outside the station.
sceneCN: 这里 accost 是「上前搭话、拦住」（第 1 个义项：以冒失或不受欢迎的方式接近并开口）；句意为一名陌生人在车站外拦住他。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加过去分词后缀构成，义为「被拦住的」
由本词加现在分词后缀构成，名词化后义为「拦截搭话的行为」

senses.title: To approach and speak boldly
senses.definition: to come up to someone and speak first, often when it is unwelcome
senses.definitionCN: 主动走到某人面前开口，且常不受欢迎
senses.example: A reporter accosted the minister at the entrance.
senses.exampleCN: 一名记者在入口处拦住部长提问。
senses.why: The word came through French from Latin accostare, 'to come to the side of'; the first move is physical, standing beside someone.
senses.whyCN: 这个词经法语来自拉丁语 accostare（走到……旁边）；第一个动作是物理的，站到别人身侧。

senses.title: To solicit or beg persistently
senses.definition: to approach people repeatedly to beg, sell, or solicit
senses.definitionCN: 反复接近他人以乞讨、兜售或拉客
senses.example: He was accosted by touts at every corner of the market.
senses.exampleCN: 市场上的每个转角都有拉客者缠上他。
senses.why: When the approach comes with a demand, the neutral 'come beside' hardens into pestering, the sense most common in city scenes.
senses.whyCN: 当接近伴随索取，中性的「走到旁边」就硬化为纠缠，这是城市场景中最常见的用法。

intro.en: Accost reached English through Old French from Latin accostare, 'to come to the side of', related to costa, 'rib, side'.
intro.cn: accost 经古法语来自拉丁语 accostare（走到旁边），与 costa（肋骨、侧边）相关。

items.en: costa meant 'rib, side', the root of coast and accost.
items.cn: costa 意为「肋骨、侧边」，是 coast 与 accost 的词根。

items.en: The prefix ad- meant 'to, toward'.
items.cn: 前缀 ad- 意为「向」。

items.en: accostare meant 'to come up to the side of' someone.
items.cn: accostare 意为「走到某人旁边」。

items.en: acooster meant 'to approach, come alongside'.
items.cn: acooster 意为「接近、靠到旁边」。

items.en: English accost first meant to come alongside a ship or a person.
items.cn: 英语 accost 最初指靠到船或人的旁边。

items.en: Modern usage narrows it to speaking first, usually unwanted.
items.cn: 现代用法收窄为主动开口，且通常不受欢迎。

note.en: The first group gathers the participle and the related coast word; the second gathers verbs for approaching people.
note.cn: 第一组收分词与相关 coast 词；第二组收表示接近他人的动词。

entries.definition: The past participle, often used in news reports.
entries.definitionCN: 过去分词，常见于新闻报道。

entries.definition: The land beside the sea, from the Latin word for side.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「海岸」，来自拉丁语「侧边」一词。

entries.definition: The present participle, as in accosting passers-by.
entries.definitionCN: 现在分词，如 accosting passers-by。

entries.definition: A verb meaning to come near someone.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「接近」。

entries.definition: A verb meaning to stop someone and force a conversation.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「拦住某人硬要交谈」。

entries.definition: A verb meaning to stop someone on their way.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「半路拦阻」。

entries.definition: A verb meaning to trouble someone repeatedly.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「反复骚扰」。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the 'to the side' origin and the street scenes; the abstract hooks picture someone stepping into your path.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用「到旁边」来源与街头场景；抽象记忆点想象有人横跨一步挡在你路上。

normal.en: Accost is 'to the side': Latin costa means rib or side.
normal.cn: accost 是「到旁边」：拉丁语 costa 意为肋骨、侧边。

normal.en: It usually implies an unwanted approach.
normal.cn: 这个词通常暗示不受欢迎的接近。

normal.en: Reporters accost ministers; touts accost tourists.
normal.cn: 记者拦住部长；拉客者缠住游客。

normal.en: The spelling has one c and double s.
normal.cn: 拼写为一个 c、双 s。

normal.en: Coast is a distant relative from the same side root.
normal.cn: coast 是同出「侧边」词根的远亲。

abstract.en: Picture a man stepping into the path of a traveller.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人横跨一步挡在旅客路上。

abstract.en: Picture a tout following a family down the street.
abstract.cn: 想象拉客者跟着一家人走过整条街。

abstract.en: Picture a microphone pushed toward a minister at the door.
abstract.cn: 想象话筒在门口被推到部长面前。

examples.en: She was accosted by a stranger asking for money.
examples.cn: 她被一名讨钱的陌生人拦住了。

examples.en: Journalists accosted the coach after the match.
examples.cn: 赛后记者们围住了教练。

examples.en: Do not accost visitors at the gate of the site.
examples.cn: 不要在工地门口纠缠来访者。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿科斯特」——横跨一步站到你旁边开口，就是拦人搭话。

root: 拉丁语 ad-（向）+ costa（侧边）→ accostare（走到旁边）；核心义是「靠到别人身侧开口」

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from a bold unwanted approach, to repeated soliciting on the street.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从冒失而不受欢迎的接近，走到街头反复拉客乞讨。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: someone stepping sideways into your path
core.cn: 核心意象：有人横跨一步挡在你面前

branches.en: A person moving up to you and speaking first.
branches.cn: 走近并先开口的人。

branches.en: Repeated approaches that demand something.
branches.cn: 反复接近并提出要求。

branches.en: The physical approach is shared by both senses.
branches.cn: 两个义项共享同一个物理接近。

branches.en: Courtesy turns to nuisance when the approach repeats.
branches.cn: 接近一旦反复，礼貌就变成烦扰。

branches.en: The same verb covers a journalist and a tout.
branches.cn: 同一个动词覆盖记者与拉客者。

intro.en: The word joins the Latin prefix ad- with the side root cost-, and its family adds a participle form.
intro.cn: 这个词把拉丁语前缀 ad- 与「侧边」词根 cost- 结合，词族另加分词形式。

latinIntro.en: Latin costa and accostare are the direct ancestors, so the Latin entries record the noun and the verb.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 costa 与 accostare 是直接祖先，因此拉丁条目记录名词与动词。

derivatives.zh: 形容词，义为「被拦住的」
名词化分词，义为「拦截行为」

definition_zh: 账户；账目；叙述；解释；说明（原因）
definition_en: a record of money held at a bank, a statement of money owed, a narrative, or to explain
core_image: 一本账册，每一笔进出都被记在一列数字里
scene: 每月底他对着银行发来的对账单核对自己记的支出，差几块钱也要查清。She checked her account before paying the rent.
sceneCN: 这里 account 是「账户」（第 1 个义项：银行保管资金的记录）；句意为付房租前她查了账户。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加表示人的后缀构成，义为「会计员」
由本词加动作后缀构成，义为「会计；记账」
由本词加形容词后缀构成，义为「负有责任的」

senses.title: A bank account
senses.definition: an arrangement with a bank to keep money and record payments
senses.definitionCN: 与银行约定保管资金并记录收付的安排
senses.example: He opened a savings account at the age of sixteen.
senses.exampleCN: 他十六岁时开了储蓄账户。
senses.why: Latin computare meant 'to reckon'; an account is a place where money is reckoned and set down.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 computare 意为「计算」；account 是资金被计算并记录的地方。

senses.title: A record of money owed or paid
senses.definition: a statement showing what is owed, paid, or received
senses.definitionCN: 显示应付、已付或已收款项的记录
senses.example: The shop sent its account at the end of the month.
senses.exampleCN: 商店在月底寄来账单。
senses.why: The written reckoning itself takes the noun, whether held by a bank, a shop, or a household.
senses.whyCN: 计算所得的文字记录本身也用这个名词，无论由银行、商店还是家庭持有。

senses.title: A narrative or description
senses.definition: a spoken or written report of an event by someone who experienced it
senses.definitionCN: 亲历者对事件的书面或口头报告
senses.example: Her account of the accident matched the video.
senses.exampleCN: 她对事故的叙述与录像一致。
senses.why: A story is also a reckoning: the teller counts up what happened and presents it in order.
senses.whyCN: 故事也是一种结算：讲述者把发生之事逐项清点并按顺序呈现。

senses.title: To explain or give a reason
senses.definition: to provide a reason or explanation for something
senses.definitionCN: 为某事提供理由或解释
senses.example: How do you account for the missing files?
senses.exampleCN: 你如何解释这些文件不见了？
senses.why: In the phrase account for, the noun's reckoning becomes an act: you settle the sum of a mystery by explaining it.
senses.whyCN: 在 account for 中，名词的「结算」变成动作：你通过解释把一桩疑问的账算平。

intro.en: Account comes through Old French from Latin computare, 'to reckon', the source of compute and count.
intro.cn: account 经古法语来自拉丁语 computare（计算），也是 compute 与 count 的来源。

items.en: putare meant 'to think, reckon', the root of compute and reputation.
items.cn: putare 意为「思量、计算」，是 compute 与 reputation 的词根。

items.en: computare meant 'to sum up, reckon together'.
items.cn: computare 意为「合计、共同计算」。

items.en: computus meant 'a reckoning, an account'.
items.cn: computus 意为「结算、账目」。

items.en: aconter meant 'to recount, give an account of'.
items.cn: aconter 意为「叙述、报账」。

items.en: English account first meant a reckoning of money, then a narrative.
items.cn: 英语 account 先指金钱结算，后指叙述。

items.en: Modern usage adds the bank account and the phrasal verb account for.
items.cn: 现代用法增加了银行账户与短语动词 account for。

note.en: The first group gathers the money and people words from the same family; the second gathers words for records and reports.
note.cn: 第一组收同族的金钱与人物名词；第二组收表示记录与叙述的词。

entries.definition: A person who keeps and checks financial records.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「会计员」，保管核对财务记录者。

entries.definition: The practice or process of keeping financial records.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「会计；记账」。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning responsible and required to explain.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「负有责任的」，须作出解释。

entries.definition: A verb and noun from the same Latin reckoning root.
entries.definitionCN: 动词与名词，同出拉丁语「计算」词根。

entries.definition: A written or spoken description of an event.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「报告」，对事件的书面或口头描述。

entries.definition: A formal account of facts or of money.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「陈述；账单」。

entries.definition: A reason given to make something clear.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「解释」，为使某事清楚而给的理由。

entries.definition: A book in which money records are kept.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「账簿」。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the reckoning root and the bank phrases; the abstract hooks picture a ledger where every line is counted.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用「计算」词根与银行搭配；抽象记忆点想象每一行都被清点的账簿。

normal.en: Account is Latin 'reckoning': computare means to sum up.
normal.cn: account 是拉丁语「结算」：computare 意为合计。

normal.en: Account for means to explain or to make up a share.
normal.cn: account for 意为解释，或占一定比例。

normal.en: On account of means because of.
normal.cn: on account of 意为由于。

normal.en: Take account of means to consider.
normal.cn: take account of 意为考虑到。

normal.en: The people words are accountant and accountable.
normal.cn: 相关人物词是 accountant 与 accountable。

abstract.en: Picture a ledger with every line added up at month's end.
abstract.cn: 想象月末把账簿每一行加总。

abstract.en: Picture a witness telling events in strict order.
abstract.cn: 想象证人按严格顺序讲述事件。

abstract.en: Picture a bank app showing one balance after rent.
abstract.cn: 想象付房租后银行应用显示的余额。

examples.en: The funds were transferred to a separate account.
examples.cn: 这笔资金被转入另一个账户。

examples.en: His account of the meeting differs from the minutes.
examples.cn: 他对会议的叙述与纪要不同。

examples.en: Sales account for half of the company's income.
examples.cn: 销售额占公司收入的一半。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿康特」——每一笔进出都记在一列数字里，账目与账户都是这个词。

root: 拉丁语 computare（计算）→ computus（账目）→ 古法语 aconter；核心义是「把发生之事清点成记录」

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from the bank arrangement, to the written reckoning, to a spoken reckoning of events, to the act of explaining.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从银行安排，走到书面结算，再到对事件的口头清点，最后是解释的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ledger where each entry is counted
core.cn: 核心意象：每一笔都被清点的账簿

branches.en: A bank arrangement that keeps a balance.
branches.cn: 保有余额的银行安排。

branches.en: The written record of money owed or paid.
branches.cn: 应付或已付款项的书面记录。

branches.en: A person's ordered report of events.
branches.cn: 个人对事件的有序报告。

branches.en: The act of settling a question by explaining.
branches.cn: 以解释把疑问算平的动作。

branches.en: Money records and stories are both entries in order.
branches.cn: 金钱记录与故事都是按序排列的条目。

intro.en: The word joins the Latin reckoning root put- with the prefix ac-, and its family adds money and responsibility endings.
intro.cn: 这个词把拉丁语「计算」词根 put- 与前缀 ac- 结合，词族另加金钱与责任后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin computare and computus are the ancestors, so the Latin entries record the verb and the noun.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 computare 与 computus 是祖先，因此拉丁条目记录动词与名词。

形容词，义为「负有责任的」

definition_zh: 会计；会计师；报账人（古义）
definition_en: a person who keeps or inspects financial records, especially as a profession
core_image: 一个人把成堆的单据按规则排进格子，最后算出总数
scene: 年末审计前，财务室整夜亮着灯，会计逐张核对发票与入库单。The accountant found two invoices that had never been paid.
sceneCN: 这里 accountant 是「会计、会计师」（第 1 个义项：负责保存或核查财务记录的人）；句意为会计发现有两张发票从未付款。

derivatives.zh: 由本词词干加名词后缀构成，义为「会计业」
同源名词，义为「会计；记账」
同源形容词，义为「负有责任的」

senses.title: A keeper of financial records
senses.definition: a person whose job is to record money received and paid
senses.definitionCN: 职业上记录收入与支出的人
senses.example: The accountant enters every sale in the ledger.
senses.exampleCN: 会计把每笔销售记入账簿。
senses.why: The -ant ending marks the person who performs the reckoning, so the accountant is literally the one who accounts.
senses.whyCN: -ant 后缀标记执行该动作的人，因此 accountant 字面上就是「做结算的人」。

senses.title: A qualified financial professional
senses.definition: a trained professional who audits, advises, and certifies accounts
senses.definitionCN: 经训练、从事审计、咨询与账目鉴证的专业人士
senses.example: Only a registered accountant may sign the audit report.
senses.exampleCN: 只有注册会计师才能签署审计报告。
senses.why: As accounting became regulated, the everyday recorder turned into a licensed expert whose signature carries legal weight.
senses.whyCN: 随着会计业受监管，日常记账者变成持证专家，其签名具有法律效力。

senses.title: One who reports or answers
senses.definition: in older use, a person who gives an account of something
senses.definitionCN: 旧用法中，对某事作出陈述的人
senses.example: The steward was called the accountant of the household's stores.
senses.exampleCN: 管家被称为家中仓物的报账者。
senses.why: Before finance narrowed the word, any person who 'rendered an account' could be called an accountant.
senses.whyCN: 在金融义收窄之前，任何「报出账目」的人都可以叫 accountant。

intro.en: Accountant is the Latin-derived agent noun of account, formed with the -ant ending for a person who acts.
intro.cn: accountant 是 account 的拉丁语式施动名词，以 -ant 后缀指执行动作的人。

items.en: putare meant 'to reckon', the root of account.
items.cn: putare 意为「计算」，是 account 的词根。

items.en: computare meant 'to sum up together'.
items.cn: computare 意为「合计」。

items.en: aconter meant 'to recount or give an account'.
items.cn: aconter 意为「叙述、报账」。

items.en: The present participle acontant named one who accounts.
items.cn: 现在分词 acontant 指报账之人。

items.en: English accountant first meant a person who reports or explains.
items.cn: 英语 accountant 最初指作报告或解释的人。

items.en: Modern usage fixes the word in finance and auditing.
items.cn: 现代用法把这个词固定在财务与审计领域。

note.en: The first group gathers the profession and practice nouns plus the responsibility adjective; the second gathers finance job words.
note.cn: 第一组收职业名词、工作名词与责任形容词；第二组收金融职位词。

entries.definition: The profession or practice of accounting.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「会计业」。

entries.definition: The activity or system of keeping financial records.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「会计；记账」。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning required to explain and answer for actions.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「负有责任的」。

entries.definition: The record or the act of reckoning behind the job.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「账户；账目」，该职业所依据的记录或计算。

entries.definition: A person who records daily financial transactions.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「簿记员」，记录日常财务交易者。

entries.definition: A person who officially checks accounts.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「审计员」，正式核查账目者。

entries.definition: An officer who manages an organisation's money.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「财务主管」，管理组织资金者。

entries.definition: A senior finance officer in a company.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「财务总监」，公司高级财务主管。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the -ant person rule and the audit scene; the abstract hooks picture a desk of receipts sorted into squares.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用 -ant 指人规则与审计场景；抽象记忆点想象桌上单据被分进格子。

normal.en: Accountant is account plus -ant, the person who does the reckoning.
normal.cn: accountant 是 account 加 -ant，做结算的那个人。

normal.en: Chartered accountant is the British professional title.
normal.cn: chartered accountant 是英式专业头衔。

normal.en: The profession is accountancy, the activity accounting.
normal.cn: 职业是 accountancy，活动是 accounting。

normal.en: In American English certified public accountant is the standard title.
normal.cn: 美式英语中标准头衔是 certified public accountant。

normal.en: Accountable is the adjective, meaning answerable.
normal.cn: 形容词是 accountable，意为需作出交代。

abstract.en: Picture a desk covered in receipts sorted into labelled trays.
abstract.cn: 想象桌上单据被分进贴标签的托盘。

abstract.en: Picture a signature at the bottom of an audit report.
abstract.cn: 想象审计报告底部的签名。

abstract.en: Picture a steward reading out the household stores.
abstract.cn: 想象管家逐一报出家中仓物。

examples.en: Their accountant advised them to delay the purchase.
examples.cn: 他们的会计建议他们推迟采购。

examples.en: A chartered accountant must sign the annual accounts.
examples.cn: 年度账目须由特许会计师签署。

examples.en: The accountant reconciled the two sets of records.
examples.cn: 会计核对了这两套记录。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿康特恩特」——把单据一张张算清的人，就是会计。

root: account（结算）+ -ant（执行者）；核心义是「以算账为职业的人」

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from the everyday recorder, to the licensed professional, to the older sense of anyone who reports.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从日常记账者，走到持证专业人士，再到旧有的「任何陈述者」义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: receipts sorted into labelled trays at month's end
core.cn: 核心意象：月末单据被分进贴标签的托盘

branches.en: The employee who records every payment.
branches.cn: 记录每笔款项的雇员。

branches.en: The certified expert whose signature carries weight.
branches.cn: 签名具有效力的持证专家。

branches.en: The old sense of a person giving a report.
branches.cn: 旧有的「作出陈述者」义。

branches.en: The same job spans routine entries and formal certification.
branches.cn: 同一职业横跨日常记账与正式鉴证。

branches.en: Reporting and reckoning were once the same act.
branches.cn: 报告与结算曾是同一个动作。

intro.en: The word is the -ant person form of the reckoning verb, and its family adds the profession and activity nouns.
intro.cn: 这个词是「结算」动词的 -ant 人物形式，词族另加职业与活动名词。

latinIntro.en: French acontant, the present participle of aconter, is the immediate model, and computare is the Latin root.
latinIntro.cn: 法语 acontant（aconter 的现在分词）是直接范型，computare 是拉丁语词根。

名词，义为「会计；记账」

definition_zh: 认证；正式认可；委派；归功于
definition_en: to officially approve an institution or course, to send an official with credentials, or to credit someone with something
core_image: 一份盖了章的证书，证明某机构或某人够格
scene: 工程系等了两年的评审，专家组走访实验室后终于出具认可文件。The programme was accredited by the national board.
sceneCN: 这里 accredit 是「认证、正式认可」（第 1 个义项：官方认定某机构或课程合格）；句意为该项目获得国家委员会的认证。

pos.zh: 认证；正式认可；委派；把……归功于

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「认证；资格认定」
由本词加过去分词后缀构成，义为「获认证的；被委派的」

senses.title: To certify officially
senses.definition: to declare officially that an institution, course, or person meets a standard
senses.definitionCN: 正式宣布某机构、课程或人员达到标准
senses.example: The laboratory is accredited to run these tests.
senses.exampleCN: 该实验室获准开展这些检测。
senses.why: Latin credere means 'to trust'; to accredit is to give credit, to declare that something can be trusted.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 credere 意为「信任」；accredit 就是给予信任，宣布某物可以被信赖。

senses.title: To send with credentials
senses.definition: to appoint an ambassador or journalist officially to a post or place
senses.definitionCN: 正式任命大使或记者到某职位或某地
senses.example: The paper accredited two reporters to the peace talks.
senses.exampleCN: 该报派了两名记者获准采访和平谈判。
senses.why: Credentials are letters of trust; sending someone accredited means sending a person the host agrees to trust.
senses.whyCN: credentials 是信任文书；派人「获认证」意味着所派之人是东道主同意信任的。

senses.title: To attribute credit to someone
senses.definition: to give someone the credit for an achievement or a discovery
senses.definitionCN: 把某项成就或发现的功劳给予某人
senses.example: The invention is usually accredited to a Swiss engineer.
senses.exampleCN: 这项发明通常被归功于一位瑞士工程师。
senses.why: Here the gift of trust becomes the gift of credit: the name that gets attached to a result.
senses.whyCN: 这里给予信任变成给予功劳：那个被附在成果上的名字。

intro.en: Accredit pairs the Latin prefix ad- with credit, from credere, 'to trust'.
intro.cn: accredit 把拉丁语前缀 ad- 与 credit 结合，credit 源自 credere（信任）。

items.en: credere meant 'to trust, believe', the root of creed and credible.
items.cn: credere 意为「信任、相信」，是 creed 与 credible 的词根。

items.en: creditum meant 'something entrusted, a loan'.
items.cn: creditum 意为「所托付之物、贷款」。

items.en: French credit carried both trust and financial credit.
items.cn: 法语 credit 兼指信任与金融信用。

items.en: English formed accredit to mean 'give credit or authority to'.
items.cn: 英语构成 accredit，意为「给予信用或授权」。

items.en: The verb came to name the sending of an accredited envoy.
items.cn: 这个动词后来指派出获认可使节。

items.en: Modern usage centres on institutional certification and attribution.
items.cn: 现代用法集中在机构认证与功劳归属。

note.en: The first group gathers the noun and participle plus credit words; the second gathers verbs of official approval.
note.cn: 第一组收名词、分词与 credit 相关词；第二组收表示官方认可的动词。

entries.definition: The official recognition given to an institution.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「认证」，给予机构的正式认可。

entries.definition: An adjective for an approved school, lab, or reporter.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「获认证的、被委派的」。

entries.definition: A document proving trust or qualification.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「资格证书」，证明信任或资格的文件。

entries.definition: Trust, praise, or a financial arrangement.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「信用、功劳、赊账」。

entries.definition: A verb meaning to confirm officially in writing.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「证明、认证」，以书面正式确认。

entries.definition: A verb meaning to give official power to act.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「授权」。

entries.definition: A verb meaning to grant official permission.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「发许可证」。

entries.definition: A verb meaning to name the cause or author.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「归因于」。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the credit root and the board phrases; the abstract hooks picture a stamped certificate handed over.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用 credit 词根与委员会搭配；抽象记忆点想象盖了章的证书被递交。

normal.en: Accredit is 'give credit': credere means to trust.
normal.cn: accredit 是「给予信用」：credere 意为信任。

normal.en: Be accredited by is the standard passive pattern.
normal.cn: be accredited by 是标准被动结构。

normal.en: An accredited representative is an officially accepted envoy.
normal.cn: accredited representative 指被正式接受的代表。

normal.en: Accredit someone with an invention means to credit them.
normal.cn: accredit someone with an invention 意为把发明归功于他。

normal.en: The noun is accreditation, common in education and hospitals.
normal.cn: 名词是 accreditation，常用于教育界与医院。

abstract.en: Picture a board stamping a certificate on a dean's desk.
abstract.cn: 想象委员会在院长桌上盖章认证。

abstract.en: Picture a reporter handed a pass at a summit door.
abstract.cn: 想象记者在峰会门口领到通行证。

abstract.en: Picture a museum label naming one engineer beneath a machine.
abstract.cn: 想象机器下方的博物馆标签写着一个工程师的名字。

examples.en: The college is accredited by the regional board.
examples.cn: 这所学院获得地区委员会认证。

examples.en: Only accredited journalists may enter the hall.
examples.cn: 只有获准采访的记者才能进入大厅。

examples.en: The discovery is often accredited to a team in Berlin.
examples.cn: 这项发现常被归功于柏林的一个团队。

branches.en: The name attached to an achievement.
branches.cn: 附在成就上的名字。

branches.en: Both senses hand out trust in a formal form.
branches.cn: 两个义项都以正式形式发出信任。

definition_zh: 认证；资格认定；认可状态
definition_en: official approval that an institution, course, or person meets a required standard
core_image: 评审团在文件上盖章，宣布这家机构可以开门
scene: 医学院每隔几年要接受一次全面检查，从课程表查到解剖室，通过后才能继续招生。The school lost its accreditation after the review.
sceneCN: 这里 accreditation 是「认证」（第 1 个义项：官方认定某机构达到标准）；句意为该校在评审后失去了认证资格。

derivatives.zh: 本词的动词形式，义为「认证；委派」
由动词加过去分词后缀构成，义为「获认证的」

senses.title: Official certification
senses.definition: the formal recognition that a body meets a required standard
senses.definitionCN: 正式承认某机构达到规定标准
senses.example: The hospital's accreditation depends on its infection records.
senses.exampleCN: 这家医院的认证取决于其感染记录。
senses.why: The -tion noun names the act of giving trust; accreditation is trust granted in writing after inspection.
senses.whyCN: -tion 名词指「给予信任」的动作；accreditation 就是检查后以书面形式给予的信任。

senses.title: The status granted
senses.titleCN: 获认可的状态；认证资格
senses.definition: the standing an institution enjoys while its approval remains valid
senses.definitionCN: 机构在认可有效期间享有的地位
senses.example: Losing accreditation would bar graduates from licensing exams.
senses.exampleCN: 失去认证资格会让毕业生无法参加执照考试。
senses.why: Once granted, the act becomes a lasting status, and the word shifts from ceremony to standing.
senses.whyCN: 一旦授予，动作就变成持续的状态，词义从仪式转向地位。

senses.title: The review process
senses.definition: the procedure of inspection and decision that leads to approval
senses.definitionCN: 导致批准的检查与决定程序
senses.example: Accreditation took eighteen months and two site visits.
senses.exampleCN: 认证花了十八个月，两次现场考察。
senses.why: The same noun can name the whole drawn-out procedure, from self-study to the final vote.
senses.whyCN: 同一个名词也可指整个漫长的程序，从自评到最终表决。

examples.en: Accreditation requires evidence of student outcomes.
examples.cn: 认证需要学生成果的证据。

definition_zh: 积累；堆积；积聚；逐渐增加
definition_en: to collect or increase gradually over time, layer by layer
core_image: 沙漏里的沙一层层落到底部，堆成小丘
scene: 阁楼角落的旧报纸一摞摞码起来，十几年没人清理。Dust had accumulated on every shelf.
sceneCN: 这里 accumulate 是「积累、堆积」（第 1 个义项：随时间逐渐聚拢增多）；句意为每个书架上都积了灰。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「积累；堆积物」
由本词加形容词后缀构成，义为「累积的」
由本词加工具后缀构成，义为「蓄电池；累积器」

senses.title: To pile up gradually
senses.definition: of things, to gather into a heap or layer over time
senses.definitionCN: 指事物随时间聚成一堆或一层
senses.example: Leaves accumulate in the gutter every autumn.
senses.exampleCN: 每年秋天落叶堆积在水槽里。
senses.why: Latin accumulare meant 'to heap up', from cumulus, 'a heap'; the verb pictures layer added to layer.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 accumulare 意为「堆起」，源自 cumulus（堆）；这个动词描绘一层加一层。

senses.title: To increase in amount
senses.definition: of money, data, or debt, to grow larger through repeated addition
senses.definitionCN: 指金钱、数据或债务经反复添加而变大
senses.example: Interest accumulates quietly on the unpaid loan.
senses.exampleCN: 未还贷款的利息在悄悄累积。
senses.why: A heap can be counted as a quantity: small additions that are invisible day by day become a large total.
senses.whyCN: 堆可以按量计算：每天看不见的小添加，最终成为一个大总数。

senses.title: To collect deliberately
senses.definition: to gather things on purpose for later use
senses.definitionCN: 为日后使用而有意识地收集
senses.example: The team accumulated ten years of weather records.
senses.exampleCN: 团队积攒了十年的气象记录。
senses.why: Human effort can speed the piling: the same verb covers both what happens by itself and what is gathered by design.
senses.whyCN: 人的努力能加快堆积：同一个动词既指自然发生，也指有意收集。

items.en: Modern usage extends it to money, data, and arguments.

definition_zh: 准确；精确度；正确性
definition_en: the quality of being correct in detail, or the degree to which a measurement or aim is exact
core_image: 靶心上的弹孔都挤在正中那一圈
scene: 射击场里，教练让大家只看落点，十发子弹几乎都贴在圆心。The accuracy of the new sight surprised the team.
sceneCN: 这里 accuracy 是「准确度、精确度」（第 1 个义项：不出错误、贴近真实的程度）；句意为新瞄准具的准确度让全队惊讶。

senses.title: Freedom from error
senses.definition: the state of being correct and free from mistakes
senses.definitionCN: 正确、没有错误的状态
senses.example: The accuracy of the translation impressed the editors.
senses.exampleCN: 译文的准确性让编辑们印象深刻。
senses.why: The -acy noun marks a quality; accuracy is the quality of a thing done with care, from Latin cura, 'care'.
senses.whyCN: -acy 后缀标记性质；accuracy 是用心做成之物的性质，源自拉丁语 cura（关心、用心）。

senses.title: Measured exactness
senses.definition: the degree to which an instrument, measurement, or aim matches a true value

senses.why: A picture can be aimed at reality the way a rifle is aimed at a target, so accurate judges the landing.
senses.whyCN: 画面可以像枪瞄准靶一样对准现实，因此 accurate 评判的是落点。

senses.title: A charge of wrongdoing
senses.definition: a statement that someone has done something wrong or illegal
senses.definitionCN: 指认某人做了错事或违法之事的说法
senses.example: His accusation surprised everyone at the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 他的指控让会上所有人都吃了一惊。
senses.why: From Latin accusare, 'to call to account', the noun names the charge laid against a person.
senses.whyCN: 源自拉丁语 accusare（传唤问责），这个名词指落在某人头上的罪名。

senses.title: The act of blaming
senses.definition: the act of saying that a person or thing is at fault
senses.definitionCN: 指出某人或某事有错的行为
senses.example: She met the accusation with a calm reply.
senses.exampleCN: 她以平静的回答应对这一指责。
senses.why: The -ation ending turns the verb into the action itself, so accusation can name the blaming rather than the charge.
senses.whyCN: -ation 后缀把动词变成行为本身，因此 accusation 也可指「指责」这个动作，而非具体的罪名。

senses.title: A formal legal charge
senses.definition: a formal charge brought before a court
senses.definitionCN: 在法庭上正式提出的控告
senses.example: The accusation was read out before the judge.
senses.exampleCN: 控告在法官面前被宣读。
senses.why: In law the word keeps its oldest sense: a formal calling to account.
senses.whyCN: 在法律中这个词保留最古老的含义：正式的传唤问责。

senses.whyCN: 源自法语 acostumer（使成惯例），这个动词把陌生之事变成习惯。

senses.title: Be used to, in the passive
senses.definition: to have become used to something, most often in the passive
senses.definitionCN: 已经习惯于某事，最常用被动形式
senses.example: She is accustomed to working night shifts.
senses.exampleCN: 她习惯上夜班。
senses.why: The passive be accustomed to freezes the result of the process, naming a settled state.
senses.whyCN: 被动式 be accustomed to 凝固了过程的结果，表示一种稳定的状态。

senses.title: Adapt the body to a place
senses.definition: to adapt the body gradually to a climate, altitude, or diet
senses.definitionCN: 让身体逐渐适应气候、海拔或饮食
senses.example: Mountaineers accustom their bodies before the climb.
senses.exampleCN: 登山者在攀登前先让身体适应。
senses.why: The same process applied to the body is called acclimatization in science.
senses.whyCN: 同一过程用在身体上，科学上称为 acclimatization（习服）。

intro.en: Accustom comes from Old French acostumer, built on a- 'to' and costume 'custom', ultimately Latin consuetudo.
intro.cn: accustom 来自古法语 acostumer，由 a-（向）与 costume（习俗）构成，最终来自拉丁语 consuetudo。

items.en: consuetudo meant 'habit, custom'.
items.cn: consuetudo 意为「习惯、习俗」。

items.en: costume meant 'habitual practice'.

items.cn: acostumer 意为「使成惯例」。

items.en: English accustom first meant 'to habituate'.
items.cn: 英语 accustom 最初意为「使习惯」。

items.en: the noun custom kept the same root for social practice.
items.cn: 名词 custom 保留同一词根，指社会习俗。

items.en: modern usage prefers be accustomed to in careful writing.
items.cn: 现代规范写作更常用 be accustomed to。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the custom root and the reflex of habit; the abstract hooks picture shoes that stop rubbing.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用 custom 词根与习惯的反复；抽象记忆点想象穿旧后不再磨脚的鞋。

normal.en: Accustom keeps custom inside: a habit is a custom worn into the body.
normal.cn: accustom 里藏着 custom：习惯就是穿进身体里的习俗。

normal.en: Accustom oneself to is the reflexive pattern.
normal.cn: accustom oneself to 是反身搭配。

normal.en: Be accustomed to names a settled state.
normal.cn: be accustomed to 表示已经稳定的状态。

normal.en: The negative is unaccustomed, common after 'not'.
normal.cn: 否定形式是 unaccustomed，常跟在 not 之后。

normal.en: Do not confuse accustom, a verb, with custom, a noun.
normal.cn: 别把动词 accustom 与名词 custom 混淆。

abstract.en: Picture new shoes that stop rubbing after a week.
abstract.cn: 想象新鞋穿一周后不再磨脚。

abstract.en: Picture a climber resting at base camp to adapt.
abstract.cn: 想象登山者在营地停留以适应。

abstract.en: Picture a farmer waking at dawn without an alarm.
abstract.cn: 想象农夫不用闹钟就在黎明醒来。

examples.en: It takes time to accustom your eyes to the dark.
examples.cn: 让眼睛适应黑暗需要时间。

examples.en: The staff were accustomed to long shifts.
examples.cn: 员工习惯了长时间轮班。

examples.en: He accustomed himself to cold water by swimming each morning.
examples.cn: 他每天早晨游泳，让自己习惯冷水。

senses.title: A salt or ester of acetic acid
senses.definition: a chemical compound formed from acetic acid and a base or an alcohol
senses.definitionCN: 醋酸与碱或醇反应生成的化合物
senses.example: Sodium acetate buffers the solution against pH change.
senses.exampleCN: 醋酸钠让溶液在酸碱度变化时保持稳定。
senses.why: The -ate ending marks the salt or ester made from an acid, so acetate is literally 'the vinegar salt'.
senses.whyCN: -ate 后缀标记由酸生成的盐或酯，因此 acetate 字面就是「醋的盐」。

senses.title: A synthetic fibre or film base
senses.definition: a material made from cellulose acetate, used for fibres, film, and plastic
senses.definitionCN: 由醋酸纤维素制成，用于纤维、胶片与塑料的材料
senses.example: The old photographs were printed on acetate film.
senses.exampleCN: 这些老照片印在醋酸胶片上。
senses.why: The chemical name shifted to the material itself: cellulose treated with acetic acid becomes a clear film.
senses.whyCN: 化学名称转指材料本身：纤维素经醋酸处理后变成透明薄片。

senses.title: A recording disc
senses.definition: a thin disc coated with acetate, used to record sound
senses.definitionCN: 表面涂有醋酸层的薄唱片，用于录制声音
senses.example: The engineer cut the session onto an acetate disc.
senses.exampleCN: 录音师把这次录音刻到一张醋酸唱片上。
senses.why: In studios the same transparent layer became a master disc for sound.
senses.whyCN: 在录音室里，同一种透明涂层成了声音的母盘。

intro.en: Acetate comes from Latin acetum, 'vinegar', with the chemical ending -ate; the acid in vinegar gave the name to its salts.
intro.cn: acetate 来自拉丁语 acetum（醋），加上化学后缀 -ate；醋里的酸把名字给了它的盐。

items.cn: acere 意为「有酸味」，是 acid 与 acetic 背后的动词。

scene: 跑了很长一段路后，小腿发沉，坐下也不见好，只能慢慢揉。A dull ache stayed in his calves all evening.

senses.title: A dull continuous pain
senses.definition: a steady, dull pain that lasts
senses.definitionCN: 一种持续、不尖锐的疼痛
senses.example: I have a dull ache in my lower back.
senses.exampleCN: 我下背部有一阵隐痛。
senses.why: Old English acan named a lasting hurt, not a sharp stab, so the noun keeps that steady quality.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 acan 指持续的疼痛而非尖利的刺痛，因此这个名词保留那种绵延的性质。

senses.title: To hurt with a dull pain
senses.definition: to feel or give a steady, dull pain
senses.definitionCN: 感到或产生持续而不尖锐的疼痛
senses.example: Her legs ached after the long hike.
senses.exampleCN: 长途步行后她的双腿酸痛。
senses.why: The verb came first; the noun was later formed from it, so ache can name both the feeling and the sufferer's state.
senses.whyCN: 动词先出现，名词后来由它派生，因此 ache 既可指感觉，也可指承受者的状态。

senses.title: To long for something
senses.definition: to want something very much, often with a hint of sadness
senses.definitionCN: 非常想要某物，常带一点惆怅
senses.example: He ached to see his family again.
senses.exampleCN: 他渴望再见到家人。
senses.why: The pain moves from the body to the heart: a longing that hurts is also an ache.
senses.whyCN: 疼痛从身体移到心里：令人难受的思念也是一种 ache。
